Penn State 8

University Park campus

  1. Must see · Penn State

    Palmer Museum of Art

    Penn State's art museum in a striking 73,000-sq-ft Allied Works building that opened June 1, 2024 at the edge of the Arboretum, nearly doubling exhibition space to 20 galleries with a store, cafe and sculpture path. Free admission; a genuine regional cultural destination.

    Look for MUS

    Palmer Museum of Art, The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by Palmer Museum of Art (official), StateCollege.com, Forbes (Chadd Scott arts coverage)

  2. Must see · American & New American · Penn State

    Penn State Berkey Creamery

    https://creamery.psu.edu/

    Food Sciences Building, Curtin Rd, University Park, PA

    Recommended by The Daily Collegian, Onward State, Wikipedia

  3. Must see · Penn State

    Old Main

    The symbolic heart of Penn State, crowning the hill above the campus mall. The 1930 Georgian building sits on the site of the original 1859 College Building of the Farmers' High School and houses the Land-Grant Frescoes by Henry Varnum Poor. Grounds open daily; the lawn is the campus's ceremonial gathering place.

    Look for CAMPUS

    Old Main, Pollock Rd, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by Happy Valley Adv. Bureau, Penn State News / psu.edu

  4. Must see · Penn State

    Nittany Lion Shrine

    One of the most photographed landmarks in Pennsylvania: a crouching mountain lion carved by sculptor Heinz Warneke from a 13-ton block of Indiana limestone, given by the Class of 1940. Reopened to visitors after a 2021-2022 site renovation; free, open-air, always accessible.

    Look for ICON

    Nittany Lion Shrine, Curtin Rd near Rec Hall, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by Penn State News / psu.edu, Centre County Encyclopedia of History & Culture

  5. Must see · Penn State

    Beaver Stadium & Penn State All-Sports Museum

    The 106,000-seat home of Penn State football and its All-Sports Museum, whose Upper and Lower galleries trace over a century of Nittany Lion athletics. Museum open Tue-Sat 10-4, Sun 12-4 (reduced winter hours; home-game-week changes); staff take guests to the club level for a view inside the bowl. Note: the stadium itself is under a multi-year renovation (Project Surge) through 2027.

    Look for SPORT

    Beaver Stadium, 1 Beaver Stadium, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by GoPSUsports (official Penn State Athletics), Penn State News / psu.edu

  6. Must see · Penn State

    The Arboretum at Penn State (H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens)

    370 acres of gardens, meadows and woodland walks a mile west of Beaver Stadium, centered on the 10-acre H.O. Smith Botanic Gardens with pollinator habitats, water features, an Overlook Pavilion and a children's garden. Free admission, open dawn to dusk daily.

    Look for PARK

    The Arboretum at Penn State, Bigler Rd & Park Ave, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by The Arboretum at Penn State (official), Happy Valley Adv. Bureau

  7. Worth the detour · American & New American · Penn State

    Brazilian Munchies

    https://www.brazilianmunchies.net/

    Pegula Ice Arena, University Park, PA

    Recommended by StateCollege.com, The Daily Collegian, Happy Valley Adv. Bureau

  8. Worth the detour · Penn State

    Frost Entomological Museum

    A free insect museum across from the Berkey Creamery, reopened in 2022 after renovation, with a live arthropod zoo and a research collection of hundreds of thousands of specimens. Open to the public 10-4 Monday-Friday; admission free.

    Look for MUS

    160 Curtin Rd, University Park, PA 16802

    Recommended by Ento, Penn State News / psu.edu

Bellefonte & Boalsburg 10

historic towns

  1. Must see · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Bellefonte Historic District

    A remarkably intact Victorian county-seat downtown along Spring Creek, listed on the National Register, built during a 19th-century iron-and-industry boom and once home to seven Pennsylvania governors. Grand houses, the 1889 railroad station and a walkable core of shops and eateries. Free, self-guided.

    Look for HIST

    High St & Allegheny St, Bellefonte, PA 16823

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Pennsylvania Wilds

  2. Must see · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Boalsburg Historic District (Birthplace of Memorial Day)

    A walkable stone-and-clapboard village that claims the first Memorial Day observance, traced to an 1864 cemetery gathering; the town center is full of shops, cafes and 18th-19th-century buildings and celebrates with a large Memorial Day weekend of events. Free, self-guided.

    Look for HIST

    Main St, Boalsburg, PA 16827

    Recommended by Visit PA (state tourism office), Historic Boalsburg

  3. Must see · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Columbus Chapel & Boal Mansion Museum

    The estate of the Boal family since 1789, whose Columbus Chapel — brought from Spain in 1909 by a Columbus descendant who married into the family — holds the explorer's admiral's desk, two relics of the True Cross and centuries of European art. Guided 90-minute tours Wed-Sun at 2pm; other times by appointment.

    Look for MUS

    163 Boal Estate Dr, Boalsburg, PA 16827

    Recommended by Columbus Chapel & Boal Mansion Museum (official), Pabucketlist

  4. Must see · American & New American · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Duffy's Tavern

    113 E Main St, Boalsburg, PA

    Recommended by Centre County Encyclopedia of History & Culture, Explorepa

  5. Worth the detour · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Talleyrand Park & the Big Spring

    Bellefonte's 3.5-acre riverside park along Spring Creek, fed by the Big Spring that pours out 11+ million gallons a day and gave the town its name ("la belle fonte"). Riverwalk, the restored 1889 passenger station, gardens and an Underground Railroad history marker. Free, open daily.

    Look for PARK

    Dunlap St, Bellefonte, PA 16823

    Recommended by Borough of Bellefonte (official), StateCollege.com

  6. Worth the detour · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Gamble Mill

    A National Register grist mill (1786/1894) on Spring Creek in Bellefonte's waterfront district, extensively restored and reopened in 2021 as a boutique hotel, restaurant and cocktail bar. A landmark on the Riverwalk; dine or stay to see the interior.

    Look for HIST

    160 Dunlap St, Bellefonte, PA 16823

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Pennsylvania Wilds

  7. Worth the detour · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    American Philatelic Center (Match Factory)

    The headquarters of the American Philatelic Society, the world's largest nonprofit stamp-collectors' organization, in the restored 1900 Pennsylvania Match Factory. Highlights include a fully reconstructed century-old general store and post office, a library and galleries. Open to visitors; check hours.

    Look for ODD

    100 Match Factory Pl, Bellefonte, PA 16823

    Recommended by Pabucketlist, American Philatelic Society (official)

  8. Worth the detour · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Centre Furnace Mansion

    The restored ironmaster's mansion of Centre Furnace — the 18th-century iron works whose owners helped found Penn State — now the home of the Centre County Historical Society and listed on the National Register. Furnished to the Moses Thompson era (1842-1891). Guided tours on posted days; grounds and gardens open.

    Look for HIST

    1001 E College Ave, State College, PA 16801

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Centre County Encyclopedia of History & Culture

  9. Closed — kept for the record · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Pennsylvania Military Museum — CLOSED

    Pennsylvania's museum of the citizen-soldier, set on the 28th Division Shrine grounds in Boalsburg. CLOSED to the public since Dec 8, 2024 for a $3.4M modernization (HVAC, geothermal, preservation systems); the reopening, once slated for Feb 2026, has slipped to 2027. The outdoor grounds and memorials remain worth a look; galleries are shut.

    Look for HIST

    51 Boal Ave, Boalsburg, PA 16827

    Recommended by PA Historical & Museum Commission (official), Wtaj News

  10. Closed — kept for the record · American & New American · Bellefonte & Boalsburg

    Creekside at the Gamble Mill — CLOSED

    https://www.gamblemillbellefonte.com/

    160 Dunlop St, Bellefonte, PA

    Recommended by StateCollege.com, Wtaj News

Happy Valley & Centre County 10

Pine Grove Mills, Lemont, Penns Valley

  1. Must see · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Mount Nittany (Mike Lynch Overlook)

    The mountain that gives Happy Valley its identity, with 8 miles of trails and seven overlooks above the valley. The short climb to the Mike Lynch Overlook (marker #3, ~0.6 mi up) gives the classic view over State College and campus; the full loop is ~4.8 mi. Limited trailhead parking in Lemont; free.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    Mount Nittany trailhead, 500 Mount Nittany Rd, Lemont, PA 16827

    Recommended by Mount Nittany Conservancy (official), Uncovering PA

  2. Must see · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Penn's Cave & Wildlife Park

    America's only all-water cavern, toured entirely by boat, plus a wildlife park with a bus safari and off-road mountain tours. Cavern tours run Feb-Dec (daily 9-4 hourly in summer); the farm-nature-wildlife park runs Apr 1-Nov (closed for winter through Mar 31). Paid admission; the cave boat tour is not wheelchair accessible.

    Look for FAM

    222 Penns Cave Rd, Centre Hall, PA 16828

    Recommended by Penn's Cave & Wildlife Park (official), Happy Valley Adv. Bureau

  3. Must see · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Black Moshannon State Park

    A 3,394-acre park atop the Allegheny Plateau built around a 250-acre lake and one of the state's finest bogs (1,992-acre Natural Area) with orchids and carnivorous plants. The half-mile boardwalk Bog Trail is the signature walk; 20 miles of trails, swimming and boating. Free day use; open year-round.

    Look for PARK

    4216 Beaver Rd, Philipsburg, PA 16866

    Recommended by PA DCNR (parks), Uncovering PA

  4. Must see · American & New American · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Meyer Dairy

    https://meyerdairyfarms.com/

    2390 S Atherton St, State College, PA

    Recommended by Centre County Encyclopedia of History & Culture, Happy Valley Adv. Bureau

  5. Must see · American & New American · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Faccia Luna Pizzeria

    1229 S Atherton St, State College, PA

    Recommended by Scmag, Onward State

  6. Worth the detour · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Rothrock State Forest

    A 96,000-acre forest of ridgelines, rhododendron valleys and mixed-oak woods wrapping the south side of the valley, prized for hiking, mountain biking and vistas (Bear Meadows Natural Area, the Mid State and Standing Stone trails). A multi-year purpose-built trail project is adding up to 47 miles; the first 7.5 opened in 2025. Free.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    Rothrock State Forest, Bear Meadows Rd, Boalsburg, PA 16827

    Recommended by PA DCNR (parks), Wpsu (PBS/NPR, Penn State)

  7. Worth the detour · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Millbrook Marsh Nature Center

    A 62-acre nature center less than two miles from campus, pairing a historic farmstead with a 50-acre limestone-fed wetland crossed by a boardwalk. Run by Centre Region Parks & Recreation; grounds free and open daily, with programs and a visitor barn. Good for families and birders.

    Look for PARK

    548 Puddintown Rd, State College, PA 16801

    Recommended by Centre Region Parks & Recreation (official), Centred Outdoors (ClearWater Conservancy)

  8. Worth the detour · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Tussey Mountain

    The valley's four-season recreation hill: 14 ski/snowboard trails in winter and a summer Fun Centre with go-karts, mini-golf, batting cages, a skate park and driving range, plus an outdoor amphitheater for concerts. Paid activities; hours are seasonal.

    Look for FAM

    301 Bear Meadows Rd, Boalsburg, PA 16827

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Ski PA (Pennsylvania Ski Areas Association)

  9. Worth the detour · American & New American · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Voodoo Brewing Co. - State College Pub

    https://statecollege.voodoobrewery.com/

    Elmwood St, Lemont, PA

    Recommended by StateCollege.com, Uncovering PA

  10. Worth the detour · American & New American · Happy Valley & Centre County

    Maine Bay & Berry Co.

    https://www.mainebayandberry.com/

    201 Elmwood St (The Barn at Lemont), Lemont, PA

    Recommended by StateCollege.com, Scmag

Altoona & Blair County 11

Horseshoe Curve, Lakemont, Tyrone

  1. Must see · Altoona & Blair County

    Horseshoe Curve National Historic Landmark

    1854 engineering marvel: a three-track loop that let locomotives climb the Alleghenies for the first time, still an active Norfolk Southern main line with a train passing roughly every half hour. Funicular (when running) or 194 steps up to the trackside viewing area; small museum and gift shop. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 1966.

    Look for ICON

    2400 Veterans Memorial Hwy, Altoona, PA 16601

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Uncovering PA, Railroaders Memorial Museum (official)

  2. Must see · Altoona & Blair County

    Altoona Railroaders Memorial Museum

    Three floors in the Pennsylvania Railroad's 1882 Master Mechanics Building telling the story of the men and women of 'Railroad City,' plus the Harry Bennett Memorial Roundhouse with a working 105-ft turntable and rolling stock. Also the ticketing gateway for Horseshoe Curve.

    Look for MUS

    1200 9th Ave, Altoona, PA 16602

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Explore Altoona, Trains Magazine / Railway Age (rail trade press)

  3. Must see · Grilled Stickies & Diners · Altoona & Blair County

    Tom & Joe's Restaurant

    Downtown Altoona's counter-and-booths diner since 1933, run by three generations of the Batrus/George family. Its griddle hotcakes are a local institution; a longtime stop on any Altoona diner crawl.

    1201 13th Ave, Altoona, PA 16601

    Recommended by Explore Altoona, Altoona Mirror (local daily)

  4. Worth the detour · Altoona & Blair County

    Lakemont Park & Leap-the-Dips

    Historic lakeside park, home to Leap-the-Dips (1902) — the world's oldest operating wooden roller coaster and a National Historic Landmark. Note: all rides have stayed closed since 2024 (declining attendance and insurance costs); for 2026 the park runs mini-golf, batting cages, courts, yard games and live-music events with free grounds admission.

    Look for FAM

    700 Park Ave, Altoona, PA 16602

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Spotlight PA (statewide nonprofit newsroom), Altoona Mirror (local daily)

  5. Worth the detour · Altoona & Blair County

    Baker Mansion (Blair County Historical Society)

    1849 Greek Revival ironmaster's mansion built for Elias Baker, now the Blair County Historical Society museum. Original Baker family furnishings — hand-carved Belgian furniture, French mirrors — and a table linked to the 1862 Loyal War Governors' Conference. Tours Fri-Sun; NRHP-listed.

    Look for HIST

    3419 Oak Ln, Altoona, PA 16602

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Atlas Obscura, Blair County Historical Society (official)

  6. Worth the detour · Altoona & Blair County

    DelGrosso's Park & Laguna Splash

    Family-owned Italian-themed amusement park founded 1946 by the DelGrosso family, whose regional pasta-sauce brand is still made on-site. 30+ rides, America's only Italian-themed waterpark, free admission and parking, homemade pasta, and the annual Italian Food & Heritage Festival.

    Look for FAM

    4352 E Pleasant Valley Blvd, Tipton, PA 16684

    Recommended by TribLIVE (Pittsburgh Tribune-Review), PA Dept. of Community & Economic Development, Visit PA (state tourism office)

  7. Worth the detour · American & New American · Altoona & Blair County

    Boyer Candy Company

    Depression-era Altoona candy maker founded by brothers Bill and Bob Boyer, who invented the Mallo Cup in 1936 — the first cup candy in America, still made downtown along with Smoothie peanut-butter cups. Factory outlet store on-site with the collectible 'Mallo Cup points.'

    821 17th St, Altoona, PA 16601

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Lancfarming

  8. Worth the detour · American & New American · Altoona & Blair County

    U.S. Hotel Tavern

    Historic Hollidaysburg hotel dating to 1835 on the Pennsylvania Canal / Allegheny Portage route, rebuilt in 1886 by a Bavarian brewmaster with a cut-block barroom added in 1905. Now a restored tavern for American plates, craft beer and cocktails inside the NRHP-listed Hollidaysburg Historic District.

    401 S Juniata St, Hollidaysburg, PA 16648

    Recommended by Explore Altoona, Nat'l Register

  9. Deep cut · Altoona & Blair County

    Historic Mishler Theatre

    1906 playhouse built by impresario I.C. Mishler and rebuilt after an early fire — one of the first U.S. buildings devoted entirely to theatre. Restored 1,900-seat, three-level venue, now home to the Altoona Community Theatre and Altoona Symphony Orchestra. NRHP-listed.

    Look for HIST

    1208 12th Ave, Altoona, PA 16601

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Mishler, Pabook

  10. Deep cut · Altoona & Blair County

    Peoples Natural Gas Field (Altoona Curve)

    Home of the Double-A Altoona Curve, named for the nearby Horseshoe Curve. A 1999 ballpark modeled on a railroad roundhouse, with a roller coaster beyond the outfield wall and a mountain backdrop — regularly called one of the prettiest parks in minor-league baseball.

    Look for SPORT

    1000 Park Ave, Altoona, PA 16602

    Recommended by Visit PA (state tourism office), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), MiLB (official Minor League Baseball)

  11. Deep cut · Altoona & Blair County

    Fort Roberdeau Historic Site

    Reconstructed 1778 Revolutionary War 'lead mine fort' in Sinking Valley — billed as America's westernmost Rev War site — with a log stockade, restored 19th-century farmhouse and barn, hiking trails and costumed interpreters. County-run park; NRHP-listed.

    Look for HIST

    383 Fort Roberdeau Rd, Altoona, PA 16601

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Explore Altoona

Central PA & the Alleghenies 6

Huntingdon/Raystown, Lewistown, Clearfield

  1. Must see · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    East Broad Top Railroad

    The oldest surviving narrow-gauge railroad east of the Rockies and a National Historic Landmark, revived by the EBT Foundation in 2020. Steam excursions behind restored locomotive No. 16, the original 1900-era machine shops and roundhouse, with track being rebuilt south toward Three Springs and Saltillo.

    Look for HIST

    421 Meadow St, Rockhill Furnace, PA 17249

    Recommended by Nat'l Register, Visit PA (state tourism office), Trains Magazine / Railway Age (rail trade press)

  2. Worth the detour · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    Lincoln Caverns & Whisper Rocks

    Two crystal caves discovered by highway blasting in 1930 and seen on a single hour-long guided tour — the only two-cave tour in Pennsylvania. Gemstone panning, nature trails and seasonal events (haunted cave, holiday tours) just west of Huntingdon on Route 22.

    Look for ODD

    7703 William Penn Hwy, Huntingdon, PA 16652

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Visit Central PA (regional CVB)

  3. Worth the detour · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    Trough Creek State Park (Balanced Rock & Rainbow Falls)

    541-acre scenic gorge where Great Trough Creek cuts through Terrace Mountain into Raystown Lake. A short trail passes 15-20 ft Rainbow Falls to Balanced Rock, a boulder perched improbably on a ledge — the park's signature landmark.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    16362 Little Valley Rd, James Creek, PA 16657

    Recommended by PA DCNR (parks), Uncovering PA

  4. Worth the detour · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    Greenwood Furnace State Park

    423-acre park on the western edge of the Seven Mountains around a six-acre lake, wrapped in the 80,000-acre Rothrock State Forest. A preserved iron-furnace historic district recalls the charcoal-iron company town that thrived here 1834-1904; swimming, camping and trailheads for backpacking and mountain biking.

    Look for PARK

    15795 Greenwood Rd, Huntingdon, PA 16652

    Recommended by PA DCNR (parks), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  5. Worth the detour · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    Bilger's Rocks

    A 170-acre community park near Grampian in Clearfield County built around 300-million-year-old Homewood Sandstone: house-sized outcrops rising up to 50 ft, riddled with arches, crevices and crawl-through passageways. Pavilion, camping and an open-air stage on site.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    1921 Bilgers Rocks Rd, Grampian, PA 16838

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Visit Clearfield County

  6. Closed — kept for the record · Central PA & the Alleghenies

    Indian Caverns — CLOSED

    Once Pennsylvania's second-largest commercial show cave, beneath a foothill of Tussey Mountain along Spruce Creek. Open to the public 1929-2016; permanently closed since 2016. Kept here as a flagged landmark — do not present as a live visit.

    Look for ODD

    5374 Indian Trl, Spruce Creek, PA 16683

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Roadside America, Atlas Obscura

34 sights and 14 places to eat across State College, the Penn State University Park campus and Centre County (Bellefonte, Boalsburg, Happy Valley), each traceable to the source that named it. The town’s canon is its own: Berkey Creamery ice cream, the grilled sticky at Ye Olde College Diner, tavern wings, Happy Valley beer, plus Old Main, Beaver Stadium and Mount Nittany.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. State College’s canon is a college town’s own: the Berkey Creamery (Penn State’s own ice cream), the grilled sticky at Ye Olde College Diner, tavern wings, Happy Valley craft beer (Otto’s, Robin Hood, Elk Creek), and the diner/breakfast institutions, sourced to the Centre Daily Times, StateCollege.com and Onward State. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — the Centre Daily Times, StateCollege.com, Onward State, the Happy Valley Adventure Bureau, Uncovering PA, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
